steps.title: Prepare Streptavidin Dynabeads
steps.instruction: Prepare and wash the Streptavidin MyOne T1 Dynabeads to be used for the affinity matrix.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend Streptavidin MyOne T1 Dynabeads thoroughly in the original bottle by gentle hand mixing.
Calculate the required amount of beads based on specified ratios and transfer them to a tube.
Collect beads on a magnet for 30–60 s.
Wash the beads once with 1 ml of 1× PBS (if using a 1.5-ml tube).
Collect beads on the magnet and resuspend in 1× PBS (volume = original bead volume minus the volume of biotinylated protein L to be added).

steps.title: Coat Beads with Protein L
steps.instruction: Incubate the beads with biotinylated protein L to prepare for antibody binding.

substeps.instruction: Incubate beads with biotinylated protein L in 1× PBS (aim for 1.5-ml total volume in a 2-mL tube) for 35 min at room temperature using gentle end-over-end mixing in a tube rotator.
Collect the protein L–coated beads on the magnet.
Wash the coated beads 5 times with 1× PBS containing 3% (w/v) BSA (IgG and protease-free). Note: 6×0.03g BSA = 0.18 g BSA.

steps.title: Bind Antibodies to Matrix
steps.instruction: Bind the specific antibodies to the protein L-coated beads.

substeps.instruction: Bind 50 μg each of 19C8 and 19F7 (100 μg total in 1 ml total volume) in low-salt buffer for 1 hr at room temperature or overnight in the cold room using gentle end-over-end rotation.
Wash the beads three times with 1 ml of low-salt buffer each time.
Resuspend the beads in low-salt buffer such that each IP receives a 200-μl final aliquot volume of beads/protein L/Ab.

Immediately before use, add filtered cycloheximide and DTT to the low-salt buffer. For 1 ml buffer: add 0.5 μl DTT (1M) and 1 μl cycloheximide (100 mg/mL); for 4 ml buffer: add 2 μl DTT (1M) and 4 μl cycloheximide (100 mg/mL).

steps.title: Store or Use Affinity Matrix
steps.instruction: Manage the prepared affinity matrix for immediate or delayed use.

substeps.instruction: Use immediately or store for up to 2 weeks at 4 °C with the addition of 0.02% sodium azide.
If stored in sodium azide, wash three times quickly in low-salt buffer before use.
If difficult to resuspend, agitate gently overnight on a tube rotator. Do not vortex after antibody binding.

steps.title: Collect and Homogenize Tissue
steps.instruction: Rapidly dissect and homogenize the sympathetic chain ganglia.

substeps.instruction: Dissect the desired tissue region rapidly and rinse in ice-cold dissection buffer.
For immediate use: Transfer tissue to a prechilled homogenizer on ice containing tissue-lysis buffer.
Maintain a ratio of ~25-50 mg of tissue per 1 ml of tissue-lysis buffer.
Homogenize in a cold room or on ice using a motor-driven Teflon-glass homogenizer at 900 r.p.m. for 12 full strokes.
Start stirring at 300 r.p.m. and slowly raise to 900 r.p.m., ensuring the pestle does not rise to the air-solution interface to avoid aeration.

steps.title: Prepare Postmitochondrial Supernatant (S20)
steps.instruction: Process the tissue lysate to obtain the S20 fraction.

substeps.instruction: Transfer lysate into a prechilled microcentrifuge tube on ice.
Centrifuge at 4 °C for 10 min at 2,000g to prepare postnuclear supernatant (S2).
Transfer S2 to a new prechilled tube on ice.
Add 1/9 sample volume of 10% np-40 (final concentration 1%, approx 100 µl) to S2, mix by inverting, and pulse-centrifuge.
Add 1/9 sample volume of 300 mM DHPC (final concentration 30 mM, approx 100 µl), mix by inverting, and incubate on ice for 5 min.
Centrifuge at 4 °C for 10 min at 20,000g to prepare postmitochondrial supernatant (S20).
Transfer S20 to a new prechilled tube. Optionally, save a 1% total volume aliquot (e.g., 10 µl from 1000 µl) and incubate at 4 °C for 16-18 h before freezing at -80 °C.

steps.title: Perform Immunoprecipitation (IP)
steps.instruction: Capture target transcripts using the prepared affinity matrix.

substeps.instruction: Thoroughly resuspend the affinity matrix (wash 3x in low-salt buffer if stored in sodium azide).
Add 200 μl of freshly resuspended beads to each S20 sample (~1,000 μl).
Incubate samples at 4 °C for 16-18 h with gentle end-over-end mixing in a tube rotator.
Collect beads with a chilled magnet; use a minifuge to spin down beads from caps between washes.

steps.title: Wash and Elute RNA
steps.instruction: Wash the captured complexes and release the RNA.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend beads in 1,000 μl of high-salt buffer and collect with a magnet.
Repeat the high-salt wash three more times (total of 4 washes), ensuring beads are visibly resuspended and mixed by pipetting at least 4 times per wash.
Remove all remaining wash buffer, remove tubes from magnet, and warm to room temperature.
Resuspend beads in 100 μl Nanoprep lysis buffer with beta-mercaptoethanol (β-ME), vortex, and incubate for 10 min at room temperature.
Collect the RNA-containing lysis buffer using the magnet.

steps.title: Purify and Analyze RNA
steps.instruction: Clean up the eluted RNA and verify its integrity.

substeps.instruction: Perform RNA cleanup using the Agilent Nanoprep kit (or equivalent) following manufacturer instructions, including optional DNase digestion and elution with buffer heated to 60 °C.
Keep purified RNA on ice and store long-term at -80 °C.
Analyze 1 μl of each sample on a Bioanalyzer 2100 using an RNA Pico/Nano chip (PicoChip range: 200-5,000 pg/ul; NanoChip range: 5-500 ng/ul).
